cards.back: A state where the derivative is zero under the model.
For a first-order exponential process, τ=1/k; it sets the characteristic response timescale.
A dimensionless ratio indicating underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped behavior.
The characteristic angular frequency of an unforced system before damping effects are considered.
Matrix of first partial derivatives of a vector field, used for local linearization.
A set where one state derivative is zero; intersections can identify equilibria.
An explicit first-order method that advances a state using its current derivative.
A system with widely separated timescales that can make explicit integration inefficient or unstable.
dC/dt = D(C_in − C) − kC with D = Q/V: first-order linear ODE.
C_ss = D C_in/(D + k); τ = 1/(D + k); 90% at τ ln 10.
Each step multiplies deviation by (1 − λh); need h < 2/λ, and h < 1/λ to avoid oscillation.
Bounds, analytic steady state, convergence on halving h and conservation.
Equilibria solve f(N) = 0; stable if f′(N_e) < 0, with recovery time constant 1/|f′(N_e)|.
N* = K(1 − h/r) exists for h < r; maximum sustained yield rK/4 at h = r/2.
Stable iff trace < 0 and det > 0; eigenvalues give fast and slow time scales.
Recovery slows as a parameter approaches the point where an equilibrium is lost.
τ dC/dt + C = c(t) with τ = V/Q; the solution is C = e^(−t/τ)[C(0) + (1/τ)∫ e^(s/τ) c(s) ds].
Step: C = c₀(1 − e^(−t/τ)), 95% at about 3τ. Ramp a t: C → a(t − τ), a constant lag aτ.
Amplitude ratio 1/√(1 + (ωτ)²), phase lag atan(ωτ), time lag atan(ωτ)/ω; faster variations are attenuated more.
Decaying input: C = c₀T/(T − τ)(e^(−t/T) − e^(−t/τ)), with a peak at ln(T/τ)/(1/τ − 1/T). Pulse = step minus delayed step (linearity).
m λ² + c λ + k = 0; ωn = √(k/m), ζ = c/(2√(km)); ζ < 1: λ = −ζωn ± jωd with ωd = ωn√(1 − ζ²); ζ = 1 critical; ζ > 1 two real roots.
δ = ln(x_n/x_(n+1)) = 2πζ/√(1 − ζ²); the peak after n cycles is e^(−nδ) of the start; it measures damping without m or k.
X = (F/k)/√((1 − r²)² + (2ζr)²), r = ω/ωn; at r = 1 it is (F/k)Q with Q = 1/(2ζ); the peak is at r = √(1 − 2ζ²); half-power width about 2ζωn.
Response phase goes 0° to 90° at resonance to 180°; above resonance the mass moves against the force, which is how soft mounts isolate vibration.
x(t) = c₁v₁e^(λ₁t) + c₂v₂e^(λ₂t); the λ are roots of λ² − Tλ + D = 0 with T = trace and D = determinant; the constants solve x(0) = c₁v₁ + c₂v₂.
D < 0: saddle. D > 0, T² − 4D ≥ 0: node (stable if T < 0). D > 0, T² − 4D < 0: spiral (stable if T < 0; center if T = 0). D = 0: line of equilibria.
λ = α ± jβ: period 2π/β, shrink factor per turn e^(2πα/β); stable if α < 0.
A saddle has one stable and one unstable direction and is very sensitive; a stable node is approached along the slow eigenvector.
dN/dt = rN(1 − N/K) gives N(t) = K/(1 + ((K − N₀)/N₀)e^(−rt)); the logit ln(N/(K − N)) is linear in t with slope r.
Half capacity at t = ln((K − N₀)/N₀)/r; 90% at ln(9(K − N₀)/N₀)/r; early doubling ln 2/r; maximum growth rK/4 at N = K/2.
With K known, two counts give r from the logit slope; a straight line of ln N on the early window gives a rate that is slightly low.
An exponential fit matches the early window and then overshoots, even beyond the capacity; a model must be tested beyond the window it was fitted on.
dx/dt = a/(1 + y²) − x, dy/dt = a/(1 + x²) − y; symmetric steady state s(1 + s²) = a; other steady states have x ≠ y.
Near a steady state, the perturbation obeys du/dt = J u with J the matrix of partial derivatives; eigenvalues with positive real part mean growth.
At the symmetric state J = [[−1, −m], [−m, −1]] with m = 2as/(1 + s²)²; eigenvalues −1 ± m; saddle (D = 1 − m² < 0) when m > 1, i.e. a > 2.
Above the threshold there are two stable asymmetric states; a tiny difference in the start decides which is reached, giving a memory of a transient signal.
y_(n+1) = (1 − λh) y_n: decays if h < 2/λ, stays positive if h ≤ 1/λ; between 1/λ and 2/λ it decays with sign changes; above 2/λ it grows.
y_(n+1) = y_n/(1 + λh): positive and decaying for any h, but only first-order accurate; nonlinear equations need an iteration at each step.
Ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue magnitude; explicit methods are limited by the largest, the time scale of interest is set by the smallest.
K_m ln(S₀/S) + (S₀ − S) = V_max t; initial rate V_max S₀/(K_m + S₀); explicit Euler stays positive near S = 0 only for h ≤ K_m/V_max.
Count the replicate wells at each time and average them; replicates are not extra time points.
A line of N on t and a line of ln N on t can both fit the early window; the line reaches zero at intercept/(−slope), the exponential never does.
Compare predictions with later observations: a model can stay positive and still be wrong in structure, for example if part of the population decays more slowly.
Hold out later data, use independent later experiments, refine numerical steps and flag impossible values instead of clipping them.
A negative count comes from the model (a form such as constant loss that crosses zero, used beyond its window) or from the numerics (an explicit step above 1/k), and the checks differ.
A fitted line N = a − bt reaches zero at a/b; a good fit in the window does not make the form valid outside it. Loss proportional to N never reaches zero.

N_(n+1) = (1 − kh)N_n: nonnegative for h ≤ 1/k (zero at equality), decaying in magnitude for h < 2/k; large steps give wrong signs, moderate steps give wrong sizes; refine h until the result stops changing.
Hold out later data; refine the step; test on independent longer data; flag invariants (non-negativity, balances) instead of clipping; state the domain of the fit.
